A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RewardBench 2 with the same authors, benchmark design, and principal experiments. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark scores, controlled reward-model training experiments, self-preference analyses, and downstream best-of-N and PPO results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluated models and cross-benchmark results in Tables 4 and 10.

M1.justification: The best-of-four benchmark design, Ties scoring, Bradley-Terry training objective, generative-judge approaches, and downstream inference procedures remain unchanged. Additional verification and explanatory details do not introduce a new model or algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds auxiliary evaluation on RM-Bench and PPE's human-preference and correctness sets, extending coverage to their prompt-response pools and preference judgments. The six RewardBench 2 domains, training mixtures, and downstream tasks remain. The IFEval-OOD-to-IFBench name and citation update does not establish changed instruction-following data.

E2.justification: Table 3 substantially revises the reported comparator set, adding Skywork Reward V2 models, both ContextualAI LMUnit models, PGRM, SARM, and non-preview Gemini variants; numerous earlier entries disappear from this table. Tables 4 and 10 also introduce actual comparisons with RM-Bench and PPE, previously discussed without these evaluations.

E3.justification: Reported Safety verification increases from half the examples in v1 Appendix E.4 to all examples in v2 Appendix G.4. Section 3 corrects the final prompt count from 1,876 to 1,865, matching the unchanged Table 2; this does not establish sample deletion. New cross-benchmark analyses use the existing 17-model PPO cohort, while the principal training and downstream protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.1 and M add analyses of agreement between benchmarks and whether the on-/off-policy PPO pattern also appears with other benchmark scores. This extends the diagnostic analysis while retaining the existing epoch, base-model, self-preference, and factuality-construction investigations.

E5.justification: The existing standard-deviation error bars and references to selecting models across hyperparameters and seeds are retained. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported; additional Pearson correlations extend the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds substantial results and changes the displayed leader from Gemini Flash preview at 77.2 to Skywork Reward V2 Llama 3.1 8B at 84.1, involving different models rather than a same-model improvement. Tables 4 and 10 add benchmark correlations and scores. Some new Table 10 scores conflict with retained results: model 10 scores 41.4 there versus 42.0 in Figure 4 and Table 9.

T1.justification: The Bradley-Terry probability and loss formulations and best-of-N selection equations are unchanged. The expanded Ties discussion supplies conceptual motivation without revising its mathematical definition or adding formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims priority for identifying the on-/off-policy factor in PPO performance in Section 5.2, strengthening the novelty claim around an existing finding. The benchmark contribution and four principal contributions listed in the introduction otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 expands the Ties interpretation to discuss confidence ordering and preserving diversity among correct responses during RLHF. It also interprets the new comparisons as showing that limited PPO predictiveness extends beyond RewardBench 2, and explains weaker agreement with PPE's human-preference component.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents Factuality spot checks and per-example Precise IF verification, and changes reported hardware from A100 GPUs at Cirrascale to H100 GPUs while retaining compute-time figures. Direct code, dataset, classifier, and Open-Instruct links are removed. Code/data release becomes conditional on acceptance, while Table 3 calls trained models released; these documentation changes do not establish actual resource unavailability or reruns.

R1.justification: New Appendix C elaborates distinctions from the benchmarks already summarized in Table 1, particularly prompt provenance, domain coverage, and objective versus subjective judgments. v2 adds the Pyatkin et al. IFBench reference and explicitly claims novelty for identifying the on-/off-policy factor. The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained, with localized rewriting, expanded explanations, terminology updates, and revised cross-references. v2 inserts example and comparison appendices, adds acknowledgements, and changes to author-date citations without substantially rebuilding the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds six illustrated dataset examples and two comparison tables, substantially expanding the visual presentation. Table 3 changes its displayed rows, caption, and model highlighting. The ICLR template changes headers, typography, and layout; existing Figures 1–7 largely retain their content while being resized or repositioned.

improvement.justification: The cross-benchmark analyses strengthen the empirical context for the existing PPO conclusions, while illustrated examples and reported complete Safety verification improve dataset transparency. These gains are partly offset by removed resource links, inconsistent release wording, and new Table 10 score discrepancies with Figure 4 and Table 9. The revision provides a limited net improvement rather than resolving the study's central evaluation limitations.
